extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature / scientific community (early 20th-century scientists, naturalists, and educated public)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative commentary on scientific monographs and reports (ethnography, observatory reports, archaeological finds, meteorology), highlighting methodological soundness, originality, scope, use of illustrations, and accuracy. Aimed at producing short critical reviews in a scientific journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start ethnographic study from aborigines upward
rubrics_metrics.description: Commencing at the bottom with the so-called aborigines and working upwards through the mixed tribes to the pure Indo-Aryan ("the only scientific method (too often neglected)").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer praises method of beginning with aboriginal populations and tracing mixtures toward more recent populations as the correct scientific approach for race/ethnographic questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness and synthesis of scattered information
rubrics_metrics.description: Brings together a mass of information that has hitherto been scattered through a number of not always accessible memoirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that compile otherwise inaccessible or scattered primary sources and consolidate knowledge for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firsthand acquaintance / field experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Unrivalled acquaintance with the people of the United Provinces, their customs, and their religion, makes this the most valuable section of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to authors who write from direct, first-hand knowledge of the people and area discussed; field experience increases the value of descriptive sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope and honesty about limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The thorny question of the origin of caste could not be adequately discussed without trenching on space which might more legitimately be devoted to other purposes, and he contents himself with stating his own opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reviewer may accept a limited treatment if the author acknowledges scope limits rather than overreaching; balance depth against breadth and be clear when an opinion is offered in lieu of exhaustive treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid descriptive depiction of local life
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the reader a vivid picture of the home-life of the plains villages; a type of account seldom put in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise descriptive passages that render local customs and everyday life vividly and add original, publishable observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situate subjects within broader historical/religious context
rubrics_metrics.description: Failed to take into consideration the results of the great reformation of Hinduism which swept over northern India in the sixteenth century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong work should account for major historical or religious transformations that shape the subject; neglecting such factors is a substantive omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed, sectioned treatment of topics
rubrics_metrics.description: The work is divided into sections dealing with domestic life, laws and customs, religion, folklore, and language; each subject is treated in great detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organise monographs into clear topical sections and provide thorough, detailed treatment in each to increase scholarly value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original contributions and newly recorded material
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains much new and valuable matter not hitherto recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give credit to works that present novel data, observations, or records that advance knowledge of a subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate and well-placed illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The full-page illustrations of the book are numerous and in their right places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use illustrations judiciously; images should be numerous enough and placed where they support text and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language documentation and standardisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Language has been reduced to writing; an alphabet and a fixed system of spelling (based on Welsh) have been given; the tongue now has a literature and is recognised by Calcutta University.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For linguistic/ethnographic works, producing a writing system, orthography, and fostering a written literature are important contributions facilitating academic recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observatory site suitability (clear horizon & low pollution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work restricted by the fact that the city has grown; the restricted horizon, the smoke, and the glare of the illuminated air have cut down useful work; relocation to extend activity may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate observatory reports in light of site limitations (horizon obstructions, urban smoke, light pollution) and note when relocation would improve scientific output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and agreement with independent determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of the latitude of the observatory (50° 5' 16".02) was in complete agreement with the value obtained by Prof. E. von Oppolzer from observations made in 1889–1899.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess observational results by cross-checking with independent measurements and published values; agreement supports reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of methodological appendices and explanatory material
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix contains a series of useful papers dealing with graphical explanations of sextant theory, precession, planet-transits, cometary orbit determinations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices that explain instruments, methods, or analytical procedures increase the utility of a report and help readers assess methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typological analysis for artifact dating
rubrics_metrics.description: The shape of the chips, knives, lance points, scrapers, and fragments of bone awls enables the stone-industry to be described as analogous to that of the Madelaine period of the Palaeolithic age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use artifact morphology and typology as criteria for cultural/chronological attribution, comparing shapes and types with established assemblages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material composition as cultural indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: White quartz (mainly ice-like transparent) furnished the principal part of the material; also red, yellow, and black varieties of quartz (jasper) employed in great profusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the raw materials used in tool production; material choices can characterise regional industries and distinguish cultural variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer population characteristics from artifact dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: On the whole, these implements are of small size, suited to small hands, and therefore employed by a small race of men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider artifact size when inferring user anatomy or population stature, but treat such inferences cautiously and corroborate with other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful interpretation of absence of expected periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Neolithic (polished stone axe) is entirely wanting in the island; Veddahs having made the step directly from the Older Stone Age into the Modern Age of Iron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a cultural phase is absent in the record, explicitly discuss whether this reflects real absence, sampling bias, or later replacement; avoid overreaching conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and innovate analytical techniques (isobaric mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction of the barometer to sea-level and the identification of closed isobars as cyclonic and anticyclonic areas were novelties; first to trace the course of a 'depression' across the Atlantic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value methodological innovations (e.g., standardising measurements, mapping techniques) that enable new insights and broader analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistical aggregation and correlational insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Realised that by appropriate combination of many observations it was possible to trace the interdependence of phenomena which might be affected separately by a number of independent causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciate work that aggregates large datasets and employs statistical reasoning to reveal interdependencies not apparent from single experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term averages and atlas-based presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly charts and tables representing the atmospheric circulation and monthly maps of forty-year averages developed into the compilation of an atlas of pictorial meteorology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use long-term averages and well-designed atlases or large-scale visualisations to represent climatological patterns and make them accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodical data presentation and visual design
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodical care in ordering the entries, and their arrangement as regards colour or design to bring out any salient features is characteristic of his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present data with careful organization and considered visual design (colour, layout) to emphasise salient patterns and aid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control through engaged observer networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Succeeded in eliciting from the observers an enthusiasm for accurate work; the collection and tabulation of observations supplied summaries required for international purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster and manage observer networks, promote accurate observations, and provide proper tabulation and summaries to ensure data quality and usefulness.
